entries.qa: Apology ('I'm sorry'). To get past someone or after bumping into them, Pardon! or Scuze! is more natural.
Neutral agreement ('fine/good'). OK and În regulă ('all right') are equally common; reviewer may prefer one.
Blank takes a number + persoane (feminine), so the number changes form: o persoană, două persoane (not doi). Colloquially people also say O masă pentru doi.
Masculine speaker. Feminine: Sunt alergică la ___. Literal: 'I am allergic to ___.' Noun after la is used without the article (la nuci, la lapte).
Masculine speaker. Feminine: Sunt vegetariană (veh-jeh-tah-ree-AH-nuh).
Literal: 'Without ___, please.' Noun without article (fără carne, fără gheață).
Answer to 'Aici sau la pachet?'. Fuller: Servesc aici ('I'll eat here'). Check which a reviewer finds most natural.
Delicios refers to the dish generically (masculine/neuter). About mâncarea or a feminine dish: A fost delicioasă. A fost foarte bun is also very common.
Depends on the item's gender: unul for masculine/neuter (un ceai, un suc), una for feminine (o bere, o cafea): Încă una, vă rog.
Pentru + noun without article works for places and towns (pentru Brașov, pentru aeroport). Până la ___ is also common.
Subject left implicit; can add Autobuzul ăsta / Trenul ăsta ('this bus/train'). The preposition changes for the city centre: Merge în centru? (not la).
Polite imperative. Preposition changes for the city centre: Duceți-mă în centru. A softer alternative: Mă duceți la ___, vă rog?
Următorul fits masculine/neuter vehicles (tren, autobuz). For a feminine noun (cursa, the next run): Când pleacă următoarea?
Literal: 'From which platform does it leave?' Romanian stations announce the track as linia, so De la ce linie pleacă? is equally common; reviewer may prefer it.

entries.qa: Depends on the item's gender: Îl iau for masculine/neuter (pantoful, tricoul), O iau for feminine (rochia, geanta).
Adjective agrees with the item: scump (masculine/neuter), scumpă (feminine), scumpe (plural).
Object left out so it fits any item; with an object: Pot să-l probez? / Pot s-o probez?
Pungă is a plastic/paper shop bag; a sturdier reusable bag is sacoșă.
Fuller and very natural: Aș vrea să mă tund ('I'd like to get my hair cut').
Unsure of the most natural barber phrasing. Literal: 'Just a little shortened, please.' Alternatives: Doar vârfurile ('just the ends'), Doar să le aranjați puțin.
Barbers also say pe lateral ('on the sides'); reviewer may prefer it. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Literal: 'Like in this photo.' Said while showing the photo; Uite, așa ('Look, like this') also works. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Literal: 'Tidy my beard, please.' Check this is the usual barber phrasing.
Literal: 'Help!' (the noun). The standard shout.
Literal: 'Call the police!' (polite/plural imperative). Emergency number in Romania is 112.
Literal: 'I have need of a doctor.' Medic is also common: Am nevoie de un medic.
Literal: 'Where is the pharmacy?' For the closest: Unde este cea mai apropiată farmacie?
Literal: 'It is an emergency.'
Literal: 'I have lost (to myself) ___.' Blank takes the noun with its definite article (pașaportul, cheile); no possessive needed. If stolen: Mi s-a furat ___.
Literal: 'I don't feel myself well.' Gender-neutral.
Literal: 'I must call someone.' Alternative: Am nevoie să sun pe cineva ('I need to call someone').
Blank takes a mass noun bare (Aveți apă?) or a countable noun with un/o (Aveți o hartă?, Aveți un încărcător?).
Blank takes un/o for 'a' (un bilet, o cafea) or the definite article for 'the' (camera). Costă is the same for singular and plural (Cât costă biletele?).

Safety phrase. Literal: 'I have need of ___, please.' After de the noun is bare (de ajutor, de apă) or with un/o (de un taxi, de un doctor). Gender-neutral. The doctor variant reuses need_doctor (Am nevoie de un doctor = 'I have need of a doctor'); in a real emergency the number is 112.
Blank takes vreun (masculine/neuter) or vreo (feminine) + noun, i.e. 'any': vreun bancomat, vreo farmacie. Un/o also works. Pe aici ('around here') is an equally common ending.
Matches pay_card. Blank takes the noun with its definite article (cu cardul, cu telefonul). Cash is different: Pot plăti cash? (no cu); formal: în numerar.
Blank takes a verb: bare infinitive (vorbi mai rar) or să + subjunctive (să repetați). Object pronouns go before puteți (Mă puteți ajuta?) or attach to să (să-mi scrieți).
First blank takes un/o + noun (o cafea, un ceai) or a bare mass noun (apă); after fără the noun is bare (fără lapte). Gender-neutral.
Blank takes a first-person verb in the subjunctive (să parchez, să fac poze). Reflexive/object pronouns attach to să (să-mi încarc).
Blank takes the noun with its definite article (intrarea, hotelul meu) or with un/o (un restaurant). For a person add pe: Caut pe cineva.
Matches tip_included. Blank takes the noun with its definite article. Inclus agrees: inclus (masculine/neuter), inclusă (feminine), incluse / sunt incluse (plural).
Blank takes a first-person subjunctive verb (să cumpăr, să schimb). Bare infinitive also works: Unde pot cumpăra bilete?
frumoasă to a woman, frumos to a man.

word_milk.qa: Literal: 'milk'. Allergen word; used without article after la / fără.

word_nuts.qa: Review edit: the allergen-label term for tree nuts. "Nuci" usually means walnuts only.

word_shellfish.qa: Literal: 'fruits of the sea' = seafood (shellfish, crustaceans, molluscs; usually not fish). Narrower: crustacee (crustaceans), moluște (molluscs).

word_meat.qa: Literal: 'meat'. Some people don't count chicken or fish as carne; for strict vegetarian needs, also say fără pui, fără pește.
